decisions.statement: An address is a page type and a slug parted by `/`, with a scope between where the type has one.
A string is an address only where its opening names a page type the index files.
A string whose slug or scope is not lower kebab case is no address.
A string naming no page the index lists is no address.
A page is passed over, because a page's relations are filed by the index.
A generated body is passed over, because its writer follows a rename.
An uncommitted body is passed over.
A file beside a page is judged.
A test is judged as any other code is.
Every string a body has is read rather than the specifiers alone.
Each spelling is named on its own.
An address built from anything but one plain string is not seen.

definition: the check refusing code that spells a page's address as a plain string
